Order-path behaviour change (not frozen surface): an exit sell whose free long quantity at the broker is below its order quantity is refused (row 'rejected', event dead-lettered, CRITICAL); Alpaca 'insufficient qty' is terminal instead of retried. Entries are unchanged.

Refused, not clamped: a full exit, the EOD flatten or the max-loss safety net sent while an earlier partial exit still holds shares is refused (Alpaca would reject it too); the remainder goes out on the engine's next exit cycle.

The guard narrows the duplicate-exit race but does not close it: Alpaca's position endpoint lagging a fill, or a sell placed outside the outbox worker between the read and the POST, can still produce a short sale.

Each exit makes two extra broker reads (client-key lookup, position) before place_order's own pre-check; an outage of either endpoint holds queued exits, and one through 15:58-16:00 leaves the position open until the next session's forced exit.
Undeclared payloads (manual API orders, events queued before this release) use the long-only rule read from ORGANISM_LONG_ONLY (env), not the engine's runtime toggle.
'insufficient qty' is detected by message text on a non-429 4xx; a changed Alpaca message falls back to the old retry path (the exit guard upstream still applies).
Duplicate exits after a broker delay page CRITICAL under their own headline ('DUPLICATE EXIT SUPPRESSED AT DISPATCH'), roughly one per engine re-fire per symbol.
